newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ATHLETICS-KOMAN BIDDING FOR 5,000 METRES WORLD RECORD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KOMAN BIDDING FOR 5,000 METRES WORLD RECORD.

text.p: Kenyan Daniel Komen, the world 5,000 metres champion, has asked organisers of Friday's Van Damme Memorial Grand Prix to add a race of that distance to the programme so he can try to claim the world record from his Ethiopian arch-rival Haile Gebrselassie.
Event promoter Wilfried Meert confirmed on Monday that the event would be added and said Komen would be bringing his own pacemakers.

Komen felt frustrated after last week's 5,000 metres in Zurich where Gebrselassie sat on his shoulder throughout before bursting clear on the final lap to destroy his own world record by nearly four seconds with a time of 12 minutes 41.86 seconds.
Komen felt the Ethiopian should have contributed to the front running and aims to prove that he too can break the record if given a ride.
Gebrselassie, who also holds the world best mark over 10,000 metres, drops down to the 3,000 in Brussels.
His Dutch manager Jos Hermens said that the Ethiopian was not troubled by a slight injury suffered in a car crash last Thursday and had resumed training in Addis Ababa.
The 10,000 metres will again feature a three-man battle between Moroccan Salah Hissou and Kenyans Paul Tergat and Paul Koech.
All three broke the 27-minute barrier in Brussels last year with Hissou winning in a then world record time. Gebrselassie has since regained the record but his rivals have it in their sights.
"Gebrselassie has put the bar very high, his record is an incredible time but both Tergat and Hissou have said they'll do whatever they can to attack it," Meert said.
The meeting, which offers a $25,000 bonus for world records, will feature 24 world champions, 14 Olympic champions and nine world record holders.
